- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or neutral, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above peak or use lagged mean.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-period, model often fails to correct; apply mean reversion to recent 7–14 day average.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment swings; smooth with 14-day moving average or use sentiment-weighted decay.
- If sentiment is high but price is flat or declining, model may overcorrect; reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid “sentiment-driven overbought” trap.
- When sentiment is low and price is trending up, model often ignores momentum; add 0.5–1.5% lagged momentum to forecast.
